title: Packaging decision for SIEM-ready audit export (beta): Enterprise Compliance bundle vs add-on
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Goal
Decide how SIEM-ready audit export (beta) is packaged and priced for Enterprise customers: included in Enterprise Compliance bundle vs separate add-on. Provide guidance for Sales/CS and contract language notes for beta terms.

Background
Audit export is positioned as an Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation feature (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3). Beta is behind a per-tenant feature flag and will be enabled for a small number of design partners first. Delivery semantics are at-least-once (duplicates possible) with durable buffering/retries and explicit failure states.

Why this decision is needed now
- Sales is already fielding security questionnaires and procurement asks for SIEM export (Splunk/Datadog/S3).
- We need a clear message for beta onboarding (what’s included, what’s not, and what we commit to).
- We need to avoid setting expectations of “exactly-once” or broad SIEM vendor coverage during beta.

Options considered
A) Include SIEM export in Enterprise Compliance bundle (default for Enterprise)
Pros:
- Aligns with positioning: compliance foundations (auditability, monitoring) as a baseline for regulated workloads.
- Avoids friction for customers who assume audit export is table-stakes with compliance posture.
- Simplifies enablement/beta: fewer SKU/quote permutations, faster customer onboarding.
Cons:
- Reduces ability to monetize as usage grows (high-volume audit pipelines can incur meaningful infra costs).
- Creates pressure for broader destination coverage to match “bundle-level” expectations.

B) Separate SIEM Export add-on SKU (attach to Enterprise)
Pros:
- Better cost-to-revenue alignment for high-volume tenants.
- Cleaner boundary of scope: can keep beta limited to Splunk/Datadog/S3 and explicitly say “additional sinks on roadmap.”
- Enables tiering by retention/throughput later (GA).
Cons:
- Adds friction for customers who consider audit export a compliance baseline.
- More operational complexity (SKU gating, quote/provisioning logic, usage visibility).

C) Hybrid: included in Compliance bundle up to a baseline, then paid add-on / overage
Pros:
- Matches unit economics while keeping “check-the-box” available.
Cons:
- Hard to implement for beta without metering/clear entitlement boundaries; risk of confusion.

Key constraints / assumptions
- Beta is feature-flagged; no self-serve enablement.
- We should not introduce complex metering in beta.
- Private deployments likely require additional support effort; packaging must not block Private adoption but should account for services/support cost.

Stakeholders consulted
- Security Eng: Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei (messaging on guarantees, scope boundaries)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (SLO/operability commitments for what we sell)
- Solutions Eng: Colin O'Donnell, Fatima Noor (beta onboarding friction, Private customer expectations)
- GTM input requested (AEs/SEs via Naomi): common objections and procurement patterns

Decision needed
By end of week: choose packaging for beta + provide default guidance for GA direction so Sales can speak consistently (even if pricing evolves).
acceptance_criteria:
- Written packaging decision for beta (bundle vs add-on) including rationale
- Pricing guidance suitable for Sales/CS (what we charge today, what’s TBD)
- Beta contract language notes (no SLA, at-least-once duplicates possible, limited sinks)
- Clear entitlement gating (feature flag + who can request enablement)
- Identified follow-ups for GA (metering, tiering, updated SKUs) with owners
decision:
Decision (2025-02-21)
Beta packaging: Include SIEM-ready audit export in the Enterprise Compliance bundle for the beta period (no separate add-on SKU during beta).

Rationale
- Most regulated prospects treat SIEM export of audit events as a baseline control; making it a separate add-on during beta creates procurement friction and slows learning.
- Beta is feature-flagged and limited; a separate SKU is not operationally worth it until we have stable usage patterns and a clearer cost model.
- We can preserve future monetization via GA tiering without blocking near-term adoption.

GA direction (non-binding)
- Move toward Hybrid model (baseline included in Compliance bundle, with a paid “SIEM Export Advanced” add-on for higher volume/retention/extra sinks) once metering and clearer unit economics are in place.
- Re-evaluate after 6–8 beta customers and 30 days of volume metrics (events/day, delivery latency, connector error rate).
pricing_guidance:
Beta pricing guidance
- Enterprise Compliance bundle customers: SIEM-ready audit export beta enabled at no additional charge for approved beta tenants.
- No usage-based charges during beta.
- Private deployments: treated as part of Enterprise platform fee; any incremental professional services/support should be handled via standard Private deployment SOW/support tier (not via a new SKU for beta).

Sales guidance (what to say)
- “Included in Enterprise Compliance bundle for beta design partners; GA packaging may introduce tiering based on volume/destinations.”
- “Initial sinks are Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, and S3; more destinations are on the roadmap.”

What not to say
- Do not promise “exactly-once” delivery.
- Do not promise support for additional SIEM vendors in beta.
- Do not quote a future list price; position that GA tiering will be informed by beta learnings.
contract_language_notes:
Beta contract language notes (for Legal/Sales Ops)
- Feature is Beta: provided “as-is”, may change before GA.
- No SLA for beta feature; uptime/latency SLOs are internal only.
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once; duplicates may occur. Customer is responsible for deduplication downstream (we provide dedupe keys and guidance).
- Scope limitations: supported sinks limited to Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3; filtering supported as documented.
- Security: destination credentials stored encrypted; customer responsible for securing their SIEM endpoints/tokens/keys.
- Data processing: audit event schema v1; Redwood may add fields in backward-compatible ways; breaking changes only via version bump.
- Termination: Redwood may disable beta access with reasonable notice (e.g., for platform stability or security reasons).
rollout_notes:
Entitlement / rollout notes
- Feature flag gating remains the control mechanism for beta enablement.
- Enablement requires Security Eng + SRE + PM sign-off for beta tenants (lightweight checklist) to avoid on-call surprises.
- Console UI remains behind feature flag; no self-serve enablement flows during beta.

Measurement needed for GA packaging
- Events exported per tenant/day, per-sink egress volume, average payload size
- Delivery latency distribution (P50/P95) and backlog depth trends
- Connector error rates by class (auth/throttle/5xx/schema)
- Support load (tickets per tenant, time-to-resolution)
open_questions:
- For GA hybrid packaging: what is the baseline entitlement definition (events/day, destinations count, retention window for replay tools)?
- Do we want S3 sink to be treated differently (cost profile, customer value, Private/on-prem fit)?
- How do we want to price/position advanced capabilities (replay/backfill tooling, longer retention, additional sinks, custom filters)?
- What is the minimum set of “Compliance bundle” features we must keep together for competitive parity (audit logs, export, retention, SSO/SAML, RBAC, etc.)?
comments: 2025-02-10 (Naomi Feldman): Met with Colin + Fatima. Both strongly prefer no add-on for beta; procurement friction is real and slows design partner onboarding. Private customers will ask for S3 first; don’t block with SKU complexity.

2025-02-12 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE perspective, please avoid any customer-facing SLA language for beta. If we include in bundle, ensure contract language explicitly states no SLA and at-least-once semantics.

2025-02-14 (Marcus Lin): Agree to bundle for beta. Keep messaging tight: ‘SIEM-ready export’ = stable schema + delivery guarantees (at-least-once) + secure credential handling. Avoid implying SIEM correlation content beyond what schema supports.
2025-02-18 (Naomi Feldman): Drafted beta contract notes and sent to Sales Ops for review. Waiting on feedback re: standard beta addendum language.

2025-02-21 (Naomi Feldman): Decision finalized: included in Enterprise Compliance bundle for beta; GA likely hybrid baseline+add-on once we have metering and volume data. Follow-up task to create GA packaging proposal after ~30 days of beta metrics.
